articles.title: Investigation Launched After Fire at Waste Site in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: The Environment Agency has begun an investigation into a fire at an illegal waste site in Rochdale, which required extensive firefighting efforts over the weekend.
articles.content_html:
An investigation has been launched following a fire at a waste site in Rochdale. Crews worked throughout the night on Friday, July 24, after a fire broke out off Spring Mill Walk in Smallbridge.

Firefighters were called to the scene at 8.15pm and worked until around 1pm the following day. Thick plumes of smoke were seen billowing above the area, visible for miles around. Six fire engines were deployed, and specialist equipment was used to extinguish the fire.

The Environment Agency became involved due to the large quantity of waste involved in the fire. In an update issued on August 1, the agency confirmed that the fire occurred at an illegal waste site, which is now under investigation.

Residents in the surrounding area were advised to keep their windows and doors closed during the incident. Dramatic images captured the scale of the firefighting operation that took place over the weekend.
